title: Local Evaluation of Time Series Anomaly Detection Algorithms

problem.claim: Classical precision and recall have limitations for evaluating time series anomaly detection algorithms.

gap.claim: Recent event-based metrics combine multiple desirable aspects heuristically, introduce parameters, reduce interpretability, and may be vulnerable to adversarial strategies.

contributions.claim: A theoretically grounded, robust, parameter-free, and interpretable extension to precision and recall based on affiliation between ground-truth and prediction sets.
Normalized precision and recall that quantify improvement over a random-baseline prediction using duration-based measures.
A local evaluation approach that supports fine-grained visualization and interpretation regarding ground-truth events.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors compare their proposal against public time series anomaly detection datasets, algorithms, and metrics.
The authors report theoretical properties that provide explicit expectations about affiliation-metric behavior and robustness against adversary strategies.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing evaluation metrics were developed to address limitations of classical precision and recall.
Recent metrics introduce heuristic aggregation, parameters, reduced interpretability, and adversarial vulnerabilities.
The paper proposes affiliation-based precision and recall extensions using duration measures.
The approach adds random-baseline normalization and local evaluation for fine-grained interpretation.
The authors report comparisons across datasets, algorithms, and metrics, together with theoretical properties.
